messages:
jess_infra: Heads up — after yesterday's driver rollout (~530.x) to the us-west1 GPU fleet I am seeing a cluster of nodes where MIG partitions vanished and GPU UUIDs shifted. A few affected nodes: gpu-uw1-12, gpu-uw1-17, gpu-uw1-23. Kube shows device-plugin entries but nvidia-smi reports no MIG devices on those GPUs.

sam_ops: Ugh. Which exact driver/kernel did we push? Any error from the node agent?

jess_infra: Deploy bot pushed driver-530.12 yesterday evening. Kernel is 6.1.21 on those hosts. Quick snippets from one affected node (gpu-uw1-12):
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d MIG
GPU 0:
    Product Name                    : A100-SXM4-80GB
    UUID                            : GPU-5f3a2c1b-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-abcdef123456
    MIG Mode                        : Enabled
    MIG Devices                     : No MIG devices found

$ kubectl describe node gpu-uw1-12 | grep -i nvidia
 nvidia.com/gpu.present: true
 nvidia.com/mig.present: true
```
So kubelet/device-plugin think MIG exists, but the driver reports none. Also noticed the GPU UUID in the plugin status doesn't match the nvidia-smi UUID for some GPUs (mapping drift).

leo_sre: Could be ordering or PCI bus id shuffle after driver reload — device-plugin maps by index/slot and we use cached UUIDs for assignment. If the driver reenumerated devices the mapping could break. Can you paste the device-plugin logs?

jess_infra: device-plugin log shows a bunch of handshake timeout + "failed to find device by UUID" errors. Short excerpt:
```
E0308 02:12:45.123 deviceplugin.go:245] failed to allocate device for pod/foo: lookup failed: no matching MIG device for UUID GPU-0a1b2c3d
I0308 02:12:45.456 deviceplugin.go:190] reported devices: [GPU-5f3a2c1b GPU-9b8c7d6e ...]
```

anya_hw: Any chance this is the known 530.x/MIG metadata race where the driver exposes MIG slots later in the init path and our plugin times out, creating stale state? We saw a similar race in staging but not this magnitude.

sam_ops: That sounds right. Two options: (1) restart device-plugin and kubelet on the affected nodes to force re-discover (fast, non-invasive), or (2) run our mig-recon tool that recreates partitions from saved config (safer for matching expected partitions). Which do you want to try first?

jess_infra: Let's try restart first on a single canary node (gpu-uw1-12). Command to restart device plugin and persistenced:
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-uw1-12
# or ssh + pkill device-plugin and let k8s restart it
```
I also ran mig-recon --dry-run and it reports missing partitions that match our saved profiles.

infra-bot: Deployment bot: driver-530.12 rollout status: 36/36 nodes updated in us-west1 at 2026-03-17T22:10:00Z. Manual intervention requested for 3 nodes (gpu-uw1-12, gpu-uw1-17, gpu-uw1-23).

leo_sre: If restart works we can avoid rollback. If restart doesn't fix it, plan B is to run mig-recon --apply on the node (this will re-create MIG partitions), then restart device-plugin. Note: re-creating partitions will change MIG device UUIDs again, so we'll need to re-sync our scheduling cache and drain/restart running pods on that node. Expect ~5-10m disruption per node.

sam_ops: I'll take gpu-uw1-12 canary now. I'll do restart + logs, then mig-recon --dry-run. If dry-run matches expected configs, I'll apply and restart the plugin. Posting updates in a minute.

jess_infra: Thanks. Also filing a follow-up ticket to add a short backoff/retry to the device-plugin discovery to avoid flapping when driver reenumerates. Long-term we should anchor by PCI bus ID rather than index/derived UUIDs.

sam_ops: Can confirm restart cleared the handshake error on gpu-uw1-12; device-plugin now reports the same UUIDs as nvidia-smi and MIG devices are back. Migrating one training job back onto it now.

anya_hw: Good catch. For the other two nodes let's run the same process during the maintenance window. Also schedule a small test to validate the next driver before full rollout (enable driver-rolling-canary + staged device-plugin restart).

leo_sre: Added an RFC for: "device-plugin discovery resilience + migrate mapping to PCI anchor" and linked to the postmortem. Assigning followups: @sam_ops triage + run recon on remaining nodes; @anya_hw prepare rollback artifact in case 530.x regresses further.

jess_infra: Great. Closing here once remaining two nodes are fixed. Keep this thread for updates. :thumbsup:
